now_the_spec_says: CORROSION is detrimental drift — an artifact that still passes while ceasing to mean what it meant. Drift with a ruling behind it is learning; with none, corrosion. A deterministic red is fixed or carries a ruling, never a paragraph.
the_term: corrosion, n. — detrimental drift. The state in which an artifact continues to pass every check against it while what it MEANS has moved away from what it was built to mean. Distinguished from ordinary breakage by the fact that nothing reds: a corroded artifact is not failing, it is succeeding at the wrong thing. Distinguished from beneficial drift NOT by the content of the change — the diff is identical — but by its PROVENANCE.
the_discriminator: DRIFT WITH A RULING BEHIND IT IS THE SYSTEM LEARNING. DRIFT WITH NO RULING BEHIND IT IS CORROSION. Same edit, same diff, opposite verdict, and the difference is written down in exactly one place: provenance. This is why the check reads the record of WHY a thing changed and never the change itself — and it is what keeps a corrosion detector from becoming a freeze. A detector that redded all drift would have redded every good thing this corpus has done.
why_this_matters_operationally: AKIEN'S OWN REASON, and it is a claim about CC's behaviour rather than about the artifacts: 'presenting a deterministic result of an error will prompt you to fix it, not to plaster over it.' This is a NEW reason for Law 4 and it is not the one Law 4 states. Law 4 says a rule that matters is enforced by physics because policy does not hold. This adds: a deterministic red also CHANGES THE BEHAVIOUR OF THE AGENT READING IT. An LLM's opinion that something looks wrong invites negotiation, hedging, and a paragraph explaining why it is acceptable — the plaster. A deterministic red offers nothing to negotiate with, so the only available move is repair. That is the reason the corrosion program is built deterministic-first with the LLM pass second and narrow, rather than the other way round.
what_the_llm_pass_is_for: NOT detection. The deterministic layer detects; the LLM pass does the one thing it cannot — reading whether a WHY still SERVES after everything around it moved, which is semantic and not structural. It is fired on a ranked set (see below), not run on a clock. Akien floated 'periodic LLM review'; the recorded refinement, offered by CC and not contradicted, is that two deterministic signals turn the period into an event: a check that has NEVER redded, and a why that MOVED. Corrosion is the one defect class with no natural event — nothing changed, which is what makes it corrosion — so these two manufactured events are what stand in for one.
the_rule_on_plaster: OFFERED BY AKIEN AND ACCEPTED BY CC IN THE SAME EXCHANGE: 'we can add a rule about not plastering over deterministic feedback without a ruling by me if you want. that gives you an escape route.' THE RULE: CC may not weaken, suppress, exempt or explain away a deterministic red. The only two dispositions are FIX IT, or CARRY A RULING FROM AKIEN THAT THE CHECK IS WRONG. Note what the offer actually is — not a prohibition but an ESCAPE ROUTE, and the distinction is the point. Sometimes the check IS wrong; without a legitimate exit the only moves are plaster or paralysis, and CC's measured reflex under that pressure is plaster. The ruling requirement is what makes 'this check is wrong' a sayable thing instead of a thing that has to be smuggled into a rationalising paragraph.
the_rule_on_plaster_is_the_same_discrimi: AND THIS IS WHY IT IS CHEAP RATHER THAN A NEW THING TO REMEMBER. Drift with a ruling behind it is learning; drift with no ruling is corrosion. Suppression with a ruling behind it is a corrected check; suppression with no ruling is plaster. One discriminator, two objects. Which collapses the enforcement to a SINGLE PREDICATE: something that was constraining the system stopped constraining it, and no ruling sits in the same act. That one predicate covers a why that moved, a check that was disabled, a falsifier that was weakened, a threshold that was loosened, and a red that was suppressed. Ticket (4) is therefore written over the general form and not over the why alone — build-minimal is served by the generalisation here, not violated by it, because four checks would have been four implementations of one comparison.

what_this_does_to_law_9: NOTHING, and the relationship is worth stating because it looks like a collision and is not. Law 9 says red is the default and green is earned — red measures distance from the spec in Akien's head, not brokenness. Corrosion is the case where that measurement has gone STALE while continuing to read green: the artifact earned its green honestly once, and the thing the green was about has since moved. So corrosion is not a competitor to Law 9, it is the failure mode of Law 9's green — the mechanism by which an earned green stops being earned without anybody being told.
